proffers.affordable_housing: $15,000 to Durham Dedicated Housing Fund
proffers.environmental_tree: Minimum 5% tree coverage (vs. 0% required); max 70% impervious surface; native species for any new landscape plantings
proffers.transit_infrastructure: 10-ft multi-use path along Page Road frontage; pedestrian/cyclist connection between Oak Mill Drive terminus and Page Road multi-use path (no vehicular connection to Page Road)
other_proffers: Utility extension agreement with Capital Properties of Raleigh LLC

member_justifications.stance_summary: Baker questioned why the development avoided a vehicular connection to Page Road, forming a cul-de-sac abutting Page Road with only a pedestrian connection. After confirming NCDOT was fine with omitting vehicular access and staff would enforce UDO connectivity rules at site plan, he voted in favor.
member_justifications.key_quote: Sorry if I missed this. Uh why no connection to Page Road?

member_justifications.stance_summary: Cook followed up on Planning Commission requests for green building commitments and EV charging stations. The applicant confirmed no green building or EV proffers were being made at rezoning, though EV stations would be explored if a shared parking lot is included at site plan.
member_justifications.key_quote: At the planning commission, there was some conversation about green building and potential EV chargers, and you said that you would talk to your client about that.

member_justifications.stance_summary: Rist confirmed that the developer satisfied Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission (BPT/BPAC) comments by committing to both a pedestrian/cyclist link from Oak Mill Drive and a 10-foot shared-use path along Page Road. He thanked the applicant for accommodating active-transportation connectivity.
member_justifications.key_quote: Well, thanks for being responsive to BPT's comments.

development_cases.location: 2503 and 2523 Hamlin Road (North Durham, near Eno Industrial Park)
development_cases.scale: Up to 81 single-family homes (conservation subdivision intent) on 42.61 acres
development_cases.zoning_change: RR (County) to RR (City) — translational zoning with non-contiguous annexation and UGB expansion

proffers.dps_cash: $25,000 one-time contribution (proffered prior to construction drawing approval)
proffers.affordable_housing: $25,000 one-time contribution to Durham Housing Fund (applicant projected homes starting mid-$300s vs. ~$600k by-right)
proffers.environmental_tree: 30% tree coverage; conservation subdivision intent reserving 50% open space bordering Army Corps land; Energy Star certified homes (non-binding under translational zoning)
other_proffers: $25,000 one-time contribution for a fire and emergency services grant project
Developer-funded extension of ~2,000 linear feet of gravity sanitary sewer plus public pump station sized for upstream properties

member_justifications.stance_summary: Rist noted he liked the conservation subdivision layout, lower projected price point, and cash proffers compared to 40 by-right septic homes. However, he voted no because conditions on the ground had not changed since adopting the UGB, infrastructure inside the current UGB remains strained, and expanding at the edge would open a Pandora's Box of similar requests.
member_justifications.key_quote: So, to me expanding the boundary now without still committing to making sure the infrastructure is there within the urban growth boundary seems to me is not worth expanding it further.

member_justifications.stance_summary: Caballero voted no because the project violates major comprehensive plan policies by sitting outside the Urban Growth Boundary without meeting UGB amendment criteria. While rejecting this application, she transparently cautioned neighbors that the parcel could rank high in a future scheduled UGB assessment and flagged JCCPC concerns about open-space designations on private land.
member_justifications.key_quote: I try and vote pretty consistently with our comp plan as best as possible... these are pretty big policies that aren't being met with this project.

member_justifications.stance_summary: Kopac acknowledged strong elements including 50% open space, water/sewer coverage, green building, and lower home prices. Yet he voted no because the parcel lies in a critical watershed outside the UGB, is non-contiguous, lacks a clear community benefit, and fails the comprehensive plan test for amending the place type map and UGB.
member_justifications.key_quote: However, at the end of the day for me, with the plans set as they are, this does fall in a critical watershed outside of our urban growth boundary.

member_justifications.stance_summary: Baker called the request an easy no despite some compelling features, arguing the comprehensive plan and UGB govern not only what and where to build, but when. He warned that far-off satellite annexations force city fire and police to drive through county territory at fiscal cost, and argued approving a private UGB change now puts the cart before the horse ahead of the new UDO and countywide open space plan.
member_justifications.key_quote: Our comprehensive plan, the future land use map, the urban growth boundary, they aren't just about what and where to build, but also when to build.

member_justifications.stance_summary: Williams saw value in adding housing supply at a more attainable price point, calling several parts of the project compelling at face value. Nevertheless, he voted no to maintain consistency on the Urban Growth Boundary and avoid setting an inconsistent precedent.
member_justifications.key_quote: It is outside of the urban growth boundary... I want to make sure that we're consistent, and don't want to set precedents one way and then change it another time.

development_cases.location: 81.75 acres east of George King Road and west of Crescent Drive (Southwest Durham, near I-40 & NC 54)
development_cases.scale: 1,667 to 2,294 residential units plus non-residential uses on 81.75 acres
development_cases.zoning_change: RS-20 (County) to CSD-C(D), CSD-S1(D), and CSD-S2(D) (City)

proffers.affordable_housing: Income-restricted/affordable housing commitments imposed on all residential phases (per text commitments page 4)
proffers.environmental_tree: Treat 100-year storm; exceed required UDO tree coverage; southwest natural heritage area restricted to public park, open space, tree coverage, constructed wetlands, and stormwater treatment; Energy Star standard for all residential committed on record
proffers.transit_infrastructure: Route every site plan through GoDurham and GoTriangle and build bus pad/shelter/pullout if deemed needed; CSD streetscape with sidewalks and bike lanes on both sides; greenway connecting dedicated park to 12-acre UNC Botanical Garden parcel; TIA required at every site plan phase; drive-thrus and convenience stores with gas sales prohibited
other_proffers: Dedication of land for a public park in southwest corner (subject to DPR approval)
Daycare facility installed prior to 50,000 sq ft of non-residential certificates of compliance
All townhouses to be alley-loaded
30-ft 0.6 opacity buffer along southern boundary adjacent to existing neighborhood

member_justifications.stance_summary: Cook argued that UDO Section 3.3 uses mandatory 'shall' language requiring a Traffic Impact Analysis at zoning map change rather than deferring to site plan, leaving staff no discretion to reinterpret. She also objected to incorporating a street/block diagram image into a textual development plan, moved to send the case back to planning staff, and voted no on continuance because she viewed the item as not properly before council.
member_justifications.key_quote: The statute is not unclear. Uh a traffic impact analysis is required... voting tonight would be in dereliction of our duty.

member_justifications.stance_summary: Rist noted that Highway 54 is identified for future Bus Rapid Transit in the county transit plan, accepted planning staff and the City Attorney's phased site-plan TIA interpretation, and cautioned that DPR's Investment Priority Indicator may rate the proffered parkland low priority. He stated he was ready to support the case while ultimately voting to continue it to February 16.
member_justifications.key_quote: We've asked so many things... I'm prepared to support this tonight. This has so much to recommend it.

member_justifications.stance_summary: Burris clarified that full buildout would span 15 to 20 years, confirmed that site-plan TIAs are administrative without public hearings, and argued park/open-space planning must account for that multi-decade horizon. She joined the majority to continue the public hearing to February 16.
member_justifications.key_quote: Remember that this is going to be built out over the next decade or so... so I just want to make sure that we're not removing things without fully understanding the time frame.

member_justifications.stance_summary: Kopac explained that after wrestling with the TIA issue on the Planning Commission, he found the applicant's commitment to conduct TIAs at every site plan phase over 10 to 20 years offers stronger long-term rigor than a single upfront estimate. He also praised protections for the natural heritage area, reduction from over 6,000 to roughly 2,000 units, and transit-oriented density that eases displacement elsewhere.
member_justifications.key_quote: By having that administrative process then, which could stop these additional phases without mitigating any additional traffic concerns including background traffic, it seemed to be a check that offered more sustained rigor.

member_justifications.stance_summary: After pressing the applicant during Q&A to commit on record to Energy Star residential buildings, alley-loaded townhomes, a daycare facility, and park dedication, Baker called Lee Village Center 'one of the better cases' he has seen in Durham. Citing Durham's drop from 72nd to 97th in Trust for Public Land park rankings after annexing 7,188 acres without parks, he supported continuing the hearing to February 16 for clarity on DPR park acceptance, mix of uses, TIA, and transit orientation before council surrenders leverage.
member_justifications.key_quote: This is one of the better cases that I've seen in my time in Durham. However, I also think that we are at this critical stage that we need to get it right... before we no longer have any more leverage on the site.

member_justifications.stance_summary: Caballero emphasized that Durham lacks transit mainly due to federal and state funding shortages that require dense, transit-oriented projects like Lee Village Center to qualify for competitive grants. While doubting that textual plans can resolve every development detail in advance, she seconded continuing the case to February 16 to extend grace to new council members seeking answers on parks and the TIA.
member_justifications.key_quote: You want the money from the feds to build a thing, you got to have the people there... I'm willing, since we are a new council, to extend some grace on some of my council member questions.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session December 4, 2025
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council convened for a Work Session on December 4, 2025, presided over by Mayor Williams. The council discussed administrative consent items, heard presentations on the 505 West Chapel Hill Street redevelopment options (including preservation via Preservation North Carolina), reviewed the 2025 third quarter crime report, and examined the FY 2025-2026 first quarter financial report. Several consent items were pulled for separate discussion, and Item 10 (redevelopment loan agreement with Durham Housing Authority) was referred back to staff upon request.

agenda_items.title: Council Announcements, Roll Call, and Meeting Decorum
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Williams called the meeting to order and roll call was conducted. Council members shared announcements including participatory budgeting updates, the Carolina Theater centennial campaign, and local sports events. Mayor Williams addressed decorum following disruptions at a prior meeting and announced new time limits for council member discussions.

agenda_items.title: City Manager & City Attorney Priority Updates
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager announced winter weather monitoring, introduced Starleta Tanner as the new permanent director of Community Partnerships and Engagement, and noted that DHA requested item 10 be referred back to staff. The City Attorney requested a closed session for attorney-client consultation on as-yet-unfiled litigation.

agenda_items.title: Board and Committee Appointments Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Clerk presented board and committee appointments, including Frederica Cadeno for the Participatory Budgeting Steering Committee (youth category) and Doug Pender for the Durham Convention and Visitors Bureau Discover Durham appointment.

agenda_items.title: Public Comments: Swing Pals Program
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Doug Hodges, founder and executive director of Swing Pals, spoke during Citizens Matter about the nonprofit providing mindfulness and golf resilience coaching for underserved youth in Durham public schools and thanked the council for supporting Hillendale Golf Course.

agenda_items.title: Hiring Practices Performance Audit (November 2025)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Audit Services Director Germaine presented a performance audit on hiring practices, discussing timelines, application processes, and recommendations to streamline hiring. HR manager Jim O'Donnell answered questions regarding applicant onboarding and job application requirements.

agenda_items.title: Tennis Court Lighting Purchase Contracts (Whipperwill Park & Rock Quarry Park)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council discussed purchase contracts for tennis court lighting at Whipperwill Park and Rock Quarry Park with Musco Sports Lighting LLC, focusing on Dark Sky compliance, lighting fixtures, spillover reduction, and fixture design standards.

agenda_items.title: Proposed Lease with Durham Regional Association of Realtors at 4238 University Drive
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council discussed a proposed lease agreement with the Durham Regional Association of Realtors Incorporated at 4238 University Drive, reviewing lease terms, property usage, and real estate department details.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation: Lee Village Center
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed the consolidated annexation for Lee Village Center (and related zoning/development items), discussing traffic impact analysis (TIA) requirements, UDO compliance, density thresholds, and planning commission recommendations.

agenda_items.title: Update on Redevelopment of 505 West Chapel Hill Street
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Extensive presentation and deliberation on redevelopment scenarios for the 505 West Chapel Hill Street site (Home Security Life Insurance Building). Topics included building preservation vs. demolition, estimated rehab costs ($25-30M), historic preservation covenants with Preservation North Carolina, interim activation open space, and affordable housing financing constraints (9% LIITC and parking requirements).

agenda_items.title: 2025 Third Quarter Crime Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham Police Department presented the 2025 third quarter crime report, reviewing violent crime trends through September, homicides (36 to date), domestic incidents, robberies, firearm involvement, and aggravated assaults.

agenda_items.title: Fiscal Year 2025-2026 First Quarter Financial Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented the FY 2025-2026 first quarter financial report, discussing quarterly stoplight reports, budget performance, CIP reporting, and departmental financial tracking.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session: Attorney-Client Consultation on As-Yet-Unfiled Litigation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pursuant to NC General Statute 143-318.11(a)(3), the city attorney requested and council voted to enter closed session for attorney-client consultation to discuss as-yet-unfiled litigation.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Approved unanimously (Motion by Council Member Cook)

meetings.title: Durham City Council December 1, 2025
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council held its organizational and regular meeting on December 1, 2025, celebrating outgoing council members and swearing in newly elected officials including Mayor Leonardo Williams, Council Members Matt Copac, Shannetta Burus, and Chelsea Cook. The council discussed community mutual aid and relief efforts responding to recent ICE and Border Patrol immigration enforcement actions across the region. Additionally, the council voted unanimously to adopt a zoning map amendment / UDO change for a residential planned development along with its required statutory consistency statement.

agenda_items.title: Organizational Meeting & Presentation of Certificates of Election
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Durham County Board of Elections presented ceremonial certificates of election to newly elected municipal officials, including Mayor Leonardo Williams, Ward 1 Councilmember Matt Kopac, Ward 2 Councilmember Shannetta Burus, and Ward 3 Councilmember Chelsea Cook, following the 2025 municipal elections.

agenda_items.title: Farewell Remarks and Service Recognitions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The council honored outgoing council members, particularly Ward 1 Councilmember Dedrianna Freeman, for their years of service and dedication to the city, sharing reflections on community advocacy and institutional legacy.

agenda_items.title: Election of Mayor Pro Tempore
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The council considered the appointment of a new Mayor Pro Tempore, culminating in the nomination and unanimous appointment of Councilmember Javier Caviierro as the city's new Mayor Pro Tempore, followed by the oath of office.

agenda_items.title: Council Member Announcements & Community Updates
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members shared updates on community responses to recent ICE enforcement raids in the Triangle, mutual aid and food distribution efforts by the Durham Community Care Collective, World AIDS Day, and Jordan High School's theatrical partnership with Broadway.

agenda_items.title: Discussion on Municipal Election Schedule and Costs
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Williams raised questions regarding the high cost of odd-year municipal elections and requested an analysis from the Board of Elections regarding potential shifts to even-year elections or four-year mayoral terms to evaluate turnout and fiscal impacts.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing and Zoning Map Amendment for Planned Development Residential
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The council held a public hearing on a request to amend the unified development ordinance (UDO) and rezone 3.35 acres on East Geer Street from Residential Suburban-20 to Planned Development Residential (PDR) for a 22-townhome infill development. Attorney Neil Gos presented developer commitments including environmental buffers, multi-use paths, and housing fund contributions.

votes.item_title: UDO Amendment / Zoning Map Change for Planned Development Residential
votes.discussion_detail: The Durham City Council considered an ordinance to amend the unified development ordinance by taking property out of residential suburban 20 (with Falls/Jordan watershed overlay district B and major transportation corridor I-85) and establishing it as planned development residential. Council members discussed questions regarding project boundary buffers, open space requirements, and minimizing impacts on wetlands and environmentally sensitive areas. Applicant and staff addressed follow-on questions from the planning commission, offering additional commitments on open space location and buffers not strictly required under the comprehensive plan. The motion to adopt the zoning amendment passed unanimously (7-0).

votes.item_title: NCGS 160D-605 Consistency Statement for Zoning Amendment
votes.discussion_detail: Following the approval of the zoning map change for the planned development residential project, the Council considered the statutory consistency statement required by North Carolina General Statute section 160D-605. A motion to adopt the consistency statement was duly moved and seconded. The vote was opened, closed, and passed unanimously (7-0).

development_cases.location: 1911 and 1915 East Geer Street
development_cases.scale: Up to 22 townhouse units on 3.35 acres
development_cases.zoning_change: RR and RS-20 to PDR 6.573 (Falls/Jordan Watershed Overlay District B, Major Transportation Corridor I-85)

proffers.affordable_housing: $20,000 to Dedicated Housing Fund
proffers.environmental_tree: Minimum 20% tree coverage (vs. 0% required under UDO); max 65% impervious surface; handle 100-year storm; native plant species; Energy Star specs; EV chargers; added commitment on record not to impact riparian buffer and to limit wetland impacts strictly to infrastructure while surrounding remaining wetlands with open space and tree save
proffers.transit_infrastructure: 10-ft wide multi-use path across frontage; bus stop across frontage on Route 3 if GoDurham wants it
other_proffers: 10-ft wide perimeter project boundary buffer (0.2 opacity)
3 accessible units with first-floor living and no stairs

member_justifications.stance_summary: Cook pressed the applicant's attorney to codify on the record that the riparian buffer would not be disturbed and wetland impacts along the East Geer frontage would be strictly limited to required infrastructure. She also verified whether the 22 townhomes would be for-sale with an HOA and asked the applicant to consider capping unit prices at 200% AMI.
member_justifications.key_quote: Right. So, is it safe to say that outside of the like necessary wetlands disturbance due to the infrastructure that y'all will not disturb the wetlands otherwise?

member_justifications.stance_summary: Rist highlighted the small-scale infill nature of the project on an active transit line and praised the developer's package of proffers. Citing projections that Durham needs roughly 32,000 housing units by 2029, he contrasted 22 townhomes favorably against the roughly five single-family homes allowed by-right.
member_justifications.key_quote: Yeah, so I think, you know, this is a good infill project. It's on a transit line. Um, it's a small project. Um, I appreciate the proffers.

member_justifications.stance_summary: Baker asked whether the development team would be willing to voluntarily and moderately increase its $20,000 Dedicated Housing Fund contribution. The applicant's attorney declined because his clients were not present and noted that $20,000 already approached $1,000 per unit, and Baker joined the unanimous vote in favor.
member_justifications.key_quote: I'm curious if you would be interested if your team would be interested in voluntarily moderately increasing the contribution to the dedicated housing fund.

member_justifications.stance_summary: Kopac thanked the applicant and staff for following up on his Planning Commission requests regarding a consistent 10-foot project boundary buffer and Policy 81 open space placement. He supported Cook's effort to finalize specific commitment language protecting the remaining wetlands and environmentally sensitive areas.
member_justifications.key_quote: I hope you're able to work with staff to come up with something that's very specific in that vein in order to minimize the impact on the wetlands and have as much of the open space and the environmentally sensitive areas as possible.
